html:
The Manhattan Project was the secret programme in which the United States, with Britain and Canada, built the first nuclear weapons during the Second World War. It ran from 1942 to 1946.

It grew out of the discovery of nuclear fission in Germany in 1938. Scientists, many of them refugees from Nazi Europe, feared Germany would build a bomb first. In 1939 Albert Einstein signed a letter warning President Franklin D. Roosevelt. After the US entered the war, the army took charge under General Leslie Groves.

The scale was huge. At its peak it employed nearly 130,000 people and cost about 2 billion dollars of the time. Its main sites were:

  • Oak Ridge, Tennessee, which separated rare uranium-235;
  • Hanford, Washington, where reactors made plutonium;
  • Los Alamos, New Mexico, where scientists led by J. Robert Oppenheimer designed the bombs.

On 16 July 1945 the first bomb was tested in the New Mexico desert, the Trinity test. In August 1945 two bombs were dropped on Japan (see atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki), killing well over 100,000 people, and Japan surrendered days later.

The project opened the nuclear age. Soviet spies had got inside it, which helped the Soviet Union test its own bomb in 1949 (see RDS-1 atomic test). The arms race that followed shaped the Cold War. Its methods also set a pattern for "big science" run by governments, and its spin-offs led to nuclear power.
sum: The Manhattan Project was the secret programme in which the United States, with Britain and Canada, built the first nuclear weapons during the Second World War. It ran from 1942 to 1946.
